image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile partially submerged in murky water. The view focuses on the dorsal surface of the head and upper back, showcasing the rough, armored texture of the scutes. The snout is visible at the bottom center, pointing downwards, while the body extends upwards into the water. A blurry, light-colored object (possibly a stick or tool) is visible in the top left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a point consistent with the V-shape description of a crocodile, distinct from the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears anatomically correct for the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the angle/ lighting makes it impossible to clearly see the interlocking teeth or the specific fourth tooth notch. The jaw line is visible but teeth details are obscured.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eyes are clearly visible on the top of the head (dorsal position). While the pupil shape is hard to resolve perfectly due to resolution, the placement and general appearance match the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct nostril openings are visible at the very tip of the snout, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating (scutes) and implies an elongated form extending out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the characteristic raised, bony ridges (scutes) running down the spine in organized rows. The texture is highly detailed and consistent with real crocodile skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of muddy browns and greys, and the surface texture is visibly rough and complex, not smooth or plastic-like.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal is viewed from above (dorsal view); the belly (ventral surface) is completely occluded by the body and the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are tucked against the body or submerged/obscured by the angle and water. No feet or digits are clearly visible for counting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the base of the tail/back is visible; the full length and compression of the tail cannot be verified as it extends out of the frame or into deep water.
